title: Zero-section and constant-family identifications for specialization
statement:
Use the specialization datum of [def-trf-deformation-specialization], the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and the Rees deformation of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed subscheme, and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor dimension, and the canonical base-change map on the zero section $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$ is an isomorphism
$$z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*M.$$

For a constant lift $T_D$ of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, the nearby-cycle unit $M\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}M$ is an isomorphism, and the specialization map on $\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,\omega_T)$ is the identity. More generally, if a lift $\widetilde T$ has a closed immersion $T_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde T$ over $T_D$, identical on the generic fibre and inducing an isomorphism on reductions, its Borel--Moore specialization map is an isomorphism, identified with that constant-family identity through invariance of the small etale site under nilpotent thickenings of these Noetherian $D$-schemes.

source.place: Proposition 1.4.2 (equation (1.8)); Example 1.3.3(a)--(b); reduction argument in the proof of Theorem 2.1.3(b)

proof.text: Pass to the etale representative $M'$ of $M$ by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The two directions of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] give $M'$ the same finite Tor interval and transfer an etale finite-Tor output back to the pro-etale category. The Rees lift is separated finite type over $D$, and its fibres and zero section are exactly those asserted by [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. Apply [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] to this lift and the generic pullback of $M'$: the output is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Thus the preservation assertion follows on the category specified by [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. From now through Step 6 work on the etale site; all comparison maps are the specified maps, so the resulting isomorphisms transfer back. We prove the zero-section comparison as an isomorphism on all bounded constructible etale inputs, a slightly stronger auxiliary assertion needed for truncations.

Constant-family unit. Apply [lem-trf-dnc-defect-proper-smooth-comparison] to the closed pair $(T,T)$, i.e. $X=Z=T$ and $i=\operatorname{id}_T$: part of its assertion is that the nearby-cycle unit $\theta_N:N\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}N$ of the constant lift is an isomorphism for every $N\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, with no finite Tor hypothesis. By Step 1, the unit on $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ is the comparison pullback of the unit on an etale representative, so it is an isomorphism; this is the first constant-family assertion. The zero-section map $\gamma_{X,Z,L}:z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^*}\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}i^*L\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}i^*L$ of equation (1.8) is exactly the canonical zero-section map of that node, and $C_{X,Z}(L)$ denotes its defect cone there.

Reductions. By [lem-trf-dnc-defect-proper-smooth-comparison], $C_{X,Z}$ is triangulated, compatible with restriction to open subsets, and has the proper comparison $C_{X,Z}(Rh_*L')\cong Rh_{Z*}C_{X',Z'}(L')$ for proper $h:X'\to X$ with $Z'=h^{-1}Z$, and the smooth comparison $C_{X',Z'}(h^*L)\cong h_Z^*C_{X,Z}(L)$; moreover $C_{X,Z}(j_!j^*L)\to C_{X,Z}(L)$ is an isomorphism and $C_{X,Z}(i_*N)=0$. Hence vanishing of $C_{X,Z}$ is Zariski-local on $X$, and it suffices to prove $C_{X,Z}(L)=0$ for bounded constructible etale $L$ with $i^*L=0$. For $Z=\varnothing$ the target category is zero and there is nothing to prove.

Let $b:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X\to X$ and $Z'=b^{-1}Z$. The ideal of $Z$ is finite type because $X$ is Noetherian; [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] makes $b$ proper, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies its complement with $X\setminus Z$, and [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] makes $Z'$ an effective Cartier divisor. Because $i^*L=0$, the unit $L\to Rb_*b^*L$ is an isomorphism: outside $Z$ it is the identity under that complement isomorphism, and over $Z$ proper base change in [prop-functor-package] gives zero, since $b^*L$ restricts to zero on $Z'$. Exactness [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and conservativity of geometric stalks check the isomorphism. The proper comparison of Step 3 consequently reduces the desired vanishing to $(X',Z',b^*L)$. We may hence assume that $Z$ is Cartier. By Zariski locality (Step 3), choose an affine chart $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ where $Z=V(f)$ is principal. If $B$ is generated over $k$ by $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, the surjection $k[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y]\to B$ sending $y$ to $f$ gives a closed immersion $e:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{r+1}$ whose inverse image of the hyperplane $H=V(y)$ is exactly $Z$, including its nonreduced structure. Closed direct image is exact by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] and faithful by applying the invertible closed counit of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]; applying proper comparison to $e$ reduces the assertion to $(\mathbf A^{r+1},H,e_*L)$. Thus it suffices to handle affine space with a coordinate hyperplane.

We prove $C_{\mathbf A^n,H}(L)=0$ for $H=\mathbf A^{n-1}\times\{0\}$ by induction on $n\geq1$, with all bounded constructible inputs. Step 3 reduces the input to $L|_H=0$. Apply the explicit affine-space coordinate-hyperplane case of [lem-trf-dnc-generic-zero-section-vanishing]. Since the target $L|_H$ is zero, its assertion says precisely that $C_{\mathbf A^n,H}(L)$ has zero stalk at every generic point of $H$ (a shift of the specialized restriction does not affect vanishing). Its bounded constructibility implies that the closure $Y$ of its cohomological support is a proper closed subset of $H$. For $n=1$, $H$ is a point and its sole point is generic, so this already proves vanishing and starts the induction.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3 and the base case of §3.2.4

proof.text:
For $n>1$, apply [lem-trf-constant-family-defect-finite-projection] to the proper closed subset $Y\subset H\simeq\mathbf A^{n-1}$ from Step 5. It gives a line $l\subset H$ such that $Y\to H/l$ is finite and its closure in the relative projective line avoids infinity. Put $X'=\mathbf A^n/l\simeq\mathbf A^{n-1}$ and $Z'=H/l\simeq\mathbf A^{n-2}$. Compactify $q:\mathbf A^n\to X'$ by $\bar q:\bar X=\mathbf P^1\times X'\to X'$, put $\bar Z=\bar q^{-1}Z'$, and extend $L$ by zero to $\bar L$. The projection is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], and $R\bar q_*\bar L$ is bounded constructible by [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], since $A$ is finite of order invertible in $k$. The proper comparison of Step 3 and the induction hypothesis give
$$R\bar q_{Z*}C_{\bar X,\bar Z}(\bar L)\simeq C_{X',Z'}(R\bar q_*\bar L)=0.$$
On the affine chart the defect is supported on $Y$ by open restriction (Step 3); outside it only the infinity section over $Z'$ remains. The projection lemma makes the union of these disjoint closed supports finite over $Z'$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-support-defect-conservativity] to $h=\bar q_Z$ and this union: the defect vanishes. This closes the induction. The reductions of Steps 3--4 now prove $\gamma_{X,Z,M}$ is an isomorphism for every closed pair, and Step 1 transfers the result to the original finite-coefficient category.

source.place: §3.2.4, completion of Verdier zero-section theorem, including the support/finite-projection argument

proof.text:
For the constant lift, write $\theta_L:L\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}L$ for the canonical unit, invertible by Step 2. Write $b:\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}\omega_T\to\omega_T$ for the exceptional exchange in the definition [def-trf-deformation-specialization], including the inverse constant-family comparison on the base point. Compatibility of ordinary exchange with the units, and of exceptional exchange with its adjoint mate, in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] gives $b\theta_{\omega_T}=1_{\omega_T}$: taking the mate of the ordinary unit square yields this equality by the adjunction triangle equations. The special-fibre composition/adjunction identifications are those of [prop-functor-package]. For $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$, naturality of $\theta$ gives $\operatorname{sp}(\alpha)\theta_{A_T}=\theta_{\omega_T}\alpha$. Consequently the defining Borel--Moore specialization is
$$b\,\operatorname{sp}(\alpha)\,\theta_{A_T}=b\theta_{\omega_T}\alpha=\alpha.$$
This proves the identity for the specified canonical map, with no properness assumption on $T$, and transfers to the finite-Tor pro-etale realization by Step 1.

source.place: Examples 1.3.3(a)--(b), with the constant-family unit of Step 2

proof.text:
Let $r:T_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde T$ be the closed immersion of the last clause. It lifts $\operatorname{id}_T$, and its special fibre is $r_0:T\hookrightarrow\widetilde T_0$. Closed immersions are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Apply [lem-trf-proper-specialization-borel-moore-compatibility] with $h=\operatorname{id}_T$ and $\widetilde h=r$. By [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward], $\operatorname{id}_{T*}\alpha=\alpha$: its unit and counit are those of the identity adjunctions and its composition isomorphism is the identity one. Hence for every Borel–Moore section $\alpha$,
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}(\alpha)=r_{0*}\bigl(\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}(\alpha)\bigr).$$
Thus Step 7 reduces the final assertion to invertibility of the Borel–Moore pushforward $r_{0*}$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1.3(b), final reduction paragraph

proof.text: Since $r$ induces an isomorphism on reductions, it is surjective on underlying spaces. By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism], $r$ and all its base changes are finite universal homeomorphisms. The small etale sites on the total schemes and after the strict-henselian and geometric-generic base changes are equivalent by [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence]. On the finite-type special fibres, [i-topology] makes $r_0^*$ and $Rr_{0*}=Rr_{0!}$ quasi-inverse on $D^b_{ctf}$, with invertible unit and counit. The composition isomorphism of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] identifies $r_0^!\omega_{\widetilde T_0}$ with $\omega_T$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1.3(b), final reduction paragraph

proof.text: By [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward], $r_{0*}$ sends $\beta:A_T\to\omega_T$ to the composite of the ordinary unit $A_{\widetilde T_0}\to Rr_{0*}A_T$, $Rr_{0*}\beta$, the dualizing composition identification, and the exceptional counit $Rr_{0!}r_0^!\omega_{\widetilde T_0}\to\omega_{\widetilde T_0}$. All comparison arrows are invertible by Step 9; in particular the exceptional counit is invertible because $Rr_{0!}$ is an equivalence, so its right adjoint $r_0^!$ is a quasi-inverse. Since the direct-image equivalence is fully faithful, this is an isomorphism on the Hom modules. Combined with Steps 7--8, the specialization is exactly the constant-family identity followed by this equivalence-induced isomorphism, as asserted.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1.3(b), final reduction paragraph and Examples 1.3.3
